models.name: discussion_board_system_settings
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings for the economic/political discussion board platform.

This table stores global configuration values that control the behavior and policies of the entire discussion board system. It contains settings that affect platform functionality, content policies, and operational parameters that apply across all user interactions.

Settings in this table are typically managed by system administrators and affect the entire platform rather than individual users or content. Values are usually set during initial configuration and modified only for significant policy or operational changes.

The table is designed to store configuration as key-value pairs with typed values to support various setting types. Changes to settings are tracked through the updated_at timestamp and audit fields to maintain an audit trail of configuration modifications.

Support for logical deletion allows settings to be marked as inactive without removing historical references, supporting compliance and rollback scenarios.

foreignFields.name: updated_by
foreignFields.description: Reference to the moderator who last updated this setting. {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: setting_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the configuration setting. This key is used programmatically to retrieve specific configuration values. Examples include 'max_image_size', 'allowed_file_types', 'posts_per_page', 'session_timeout_minutes'.

plainFields.name: setting_value
plainFields.description: The value of the configuration setting stored as a string representation. Different data types are stored as strings and parsed by the application according to the setting_key. For example, numeric values like '100' for maximum posts per page, or comma-separated lists like 'jpg,png,gif,pdf,doc' for allowed file types.

plainFields.name: setting_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the setting value to enable proper parsing by the application. Valid values include 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'array_string' for comma-separated values, and 'json' for structured data. This field ensures type-safe handling of configuration values.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of what the setting controls and its possible values. This documentation helps administrators understand the purpose and proper values for each configuration option without requiring code-level knowledge.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was first created in the system. This field provides an audit trail showing when settings were initially established.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was last modified. This field allows administrators to track when settings were changed and helps with troubleshooting configuration-related issues.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration setting was logically deleted. This field enables soft deletion of settings while maintaining historical references for audit and compliance purposes.

models.name: discussion_board_guest
models.description:
Guest users who can browse public content but cannot create posts or participate in discussions.

These users represent unauthenticated visitors who have read-only access to the discussion board.
Guest users provide content discoverability for search engines and casual visitors while protecting contribution
capabilities for registered users. They do not require authentication or session management as they are not
logged in.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address used by the guest for tracking and rate limiting purposes.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string for device and browser identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was first recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: last_seen_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the guest's last activity on the platform.

models.name: discussion_board_member
models.description:
Authenticated member users who can create posts with images and file attachments, comment on posts, and manage their own content.

These users represent the core community that drives discussion activity on the platform.
Members have full participation rights after registration and email verification. They can create
content, engage with other users, and manage their contributions with appropriate permissions.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique display name chosen by the member for identification in discussions.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for authentication, notifications, and account recovery.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for user authentication.

plainFields.name: is_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the member has verified their email address to activate full platform features.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft deleted (null if active).

models.name: discussion_board_moderator
models.description:
Administrative users who can review and approve posts, manage user accounts, delete inappropriate content, and configure system settings.

These users provide oversight capabilities necessary to maintain community standards and platform quality.
Moderators have elevated privileges to perform content review, user management, and system administration
tasks. They are responsible for enforcing community guidelines and ensuring appropriate content quality.

plainFields.name: username
plainFields.description: Unique display name for the moderator in administrative contexts.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address used for authentication and administrative notifications.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Securely hashed password for moderator authentication.

plainFields.name: permissions_level
plainFields.description: Authorization level determining which administrative functions this moderator can perform.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the moderator account was soft deleted (null if active).

models.name: discussion_board_member_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for member users.

Tracks login sessions for registered members to maintain authentication state and provide audit trails.
Each session is associated with a specific member and captures connection context for security monitoring.
This table supports the platform's authentication system for member users and enables session management
features such as logout and session expiration.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used during the session for security monitoring.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL that initiated the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the session initiation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or will expire (null if active).

models.name: discussion_board_moderator_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for moderator users.

Tracks login sessions for administrative moderators to maintain authentication state and provide audit trails.
Each session is associated with a specific moderator and captures connection context for security monitoring.
This table supports the platform's authentication system for moderator users and enables session management
features such as logout and session expiration.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address used during the session for security monitoring.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL that initiated the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to the session initiation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expired or will expire (null if active).

models.name: discussion_board_articles
models.description:
Articles created by users on economic or political topics.

This table stores the primary content pieces in the discussion board system. Articles can be created by members or moderators and must go through an approval process before becoming publicly visible. Each article is associated with one or more categories and can include file attachments.

Articles have a lifecycle managed through their status field, starting as 'pending' and moving to 'approved' or 'rejected' based on moderator review. The system maintains full audit trails of article changes through snapshot tables and preserves deleted content for compliance purposes.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: The member or moderator who created this article. {@link discussion_board_member.id} or {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: The primary category this article belongs to. {@link discussion_board_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: The title of the article. Must be between 5-200 characters.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The main content body of the article. Must be between 10-10,000 characters.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The current approval status of the article. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was deleted (soft delete).

models.name: discussion_board_comments
models.description:
Comments made by users on discussion board articles.

This table stores user comments on articles. Comments can be made by any authenticated user (member or moderator) and are associated with a specific article. Each comment includes text content and maintains timestamps for creation and modification.

Comments support the core engagement functionality of the discussion board, allowing users to respond to articles and participate in discussions. Like articles, comments support soft deletion to preserve discussion context while allowing inappropriate content to be removed.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment belongs to. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: The member or moderator who created this comment. {@link discussion_board_member.id} or {@link discussion_board_moderator.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The comment text content. Must be between 1-2,000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the comment was deleted (soft delete).

models.name: discussion_board_attachments
models.description:
File attachments associated with discussion board articles.

This table stores metadata for files attached to articles in the discussion board. Each attachment is linked to a specific article and contains information about the file including its name, storage path, type, and upload time. Attachments support both image and document files as specified in the requirements.

The system allows multiple attachments per article (up to 5 images and 3 documents according to functional requirements). Attachments are managed through the article lifecycle and are not directly accessible without article context.

When articles are deleted, their attachments are also removed as part of the content management process. File storage paths reference the actual files stored in the system's file storage infrastructure.

Attachments maintain traceability to the original uploader through a polymorphic relationship to either a member or moderator who created the article to which this attachment belongs.

foreignFields.name: discussion_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: The article to which this attachment belongs. {@link discussion_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original name of the uploaded file as provided by the user. This preserves the user's file naming convention while the system uses unique identifiers for actual file storage.

plainFields.name: file_path
plainFields.description: Path to the file in the storage system. This is a unique identifier generated by the system for secure file access and management.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., image/jpeg, application/pdf). Used to determine how to handle and display the file appropriately.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Used for storage management and to enforce file size limits as specified in the requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded and created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment metadata was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attachment was soft deleted. Null if the attachment is active.

models.name: discussion_board_categories
models.description:
Discussion board categories that organize articles by topic.

This table defines the available categories that can be assigned to articles. The system
is designed with exactly two categories as specified in requirements: economic and political.
Each category has a unique name and can be associated with multiple articles through the
article_categories junction table.

Categories support soft deletion to maintain historical references while allowing for
administrative management. The system can be extended with additional categories in
the future without requiring schema changes.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: The name of the category (e.g., economic, political). Must be unique across all categories.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: A detailed description of what type of content belongs in this category.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was deleted (soft delete).

models.name: discussion_board_article_categories
models.description:
Junction table linking articles to their assigned categories.

This table establishes the many-to-many relationship between articles and categories,
allowing articles to be classified under one or more categories. Each record represents
an association between a single article and a single category.

The table includes temporal fields to track when associations were created, supporting
audit trails and historical analysis of content categorization. Soft deletion is
implemented to preserve historical data while allowing for re-categorization.

This entity has primary stance because users need to independently manage these
associations, search across articles by category, and perform administrative operations
on category assignments regardless of parent context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article-category association was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article-category association was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article-category association was deleted (soft delete).
